exercises.title: Power, Energy, and Thermal Basics: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: A device dissipates 1.2 W and has a junction-to-ambient thermal resistance of 45 °C/W in a 30 °C ambient. What is the estimated junction temperature?
hints: Rise = power × thermal resistance, then add ambient.

exercises.title: Power, Energy, and Thermal Basics: worked analysis
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Estimate junction temperature for a device dissipating 1.2 W with 45 °C/W junction-to-ambient at 30 °C ambient.

Show assumptions, equations, units, standard-value choices, ratings, tolerance effects, and the measurements that would verify the result.
checklist: I drew or described the complete source and return path.
I carried units and checked the order of magnitude.
I checked ratings and at least one worst-case condition.
I wrote an observable verification step before viewing the solution.
hints: Start with a symbolic relationship before substituting numbers.
Separate typical behavior from guaranteed limits and add measurement tolerance.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference solution

Temperature rise is 1.2 W × 45 °C/W = 54 °C. At 30 °C ambient the estimated junction temperature is 84 °C. This is acceptable only if it remains below the recommended operating limit with interface and airflow uncertainty; absolute maximum junction temperature is not a design target.

The governing principle is: **close the electrical and thermal budgets together rather than treating rated power as a target**. Define every reference direction and convert values to coherent SI units. Compare the result with component ratings and standard available values, then report a bounded expectation that includes tolerance, temperature, supply variation, and instrument loading.

### Verification evidence

1. Power off and confirm wiring, polarity, and discharge state.
2. Configure a conservative current limit.
3. Predict source current and the critical node voltages or waveform features.
4. Power on and compare the first measurement with the bounded prediction.
5. Stop if current, temperature, smell, or waveform exceeds the safe bound.

The notebook should make both the reasoning and bench test independently reproducible.

exercises.title: Power, Energy, and Thermal Basics: measurement and fault investigation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Plan or perform a low-voltage investigation of **overloaded resistor, inadequate copper area, missing derating, optimistic efficiency**. Record a safe setup, predicted healthy evidence, observed evidence, one hypothesis at a time, and the final verification.
checklist: I documented the de-energized inspection and safe current limit.
I recorded expected healthy readings before measuring.
I used one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.
I included final evidence that distinguishes cause from symptom.
hints: Measure the supply current and block boundaries before probing internal details.
Change only one condition between measurements.
